vision.name: Tamagotui
vision.description: Tamagotui is a local-first, always-visible virtual pet that lives on the edge of your screen and grows based on your real developer activity — commits, CLI usage, and custom events. It turns invisible daily coding grind into an ambient, emotionally engaging creature you glance at instead of a dashboard you have to seek out, complete with growth stages, idle decay, and an optional burnout mechanic that nudges you toward healthier work habits.
goals: Provide an ambient, glanceable representation of developer productivity without requiring active dashboard checking
Turn real dev signals (commits, CLI usage, deploys) into meaningful, emotionally engaging gamification
Ship a fully offline, local-first, zero-dependency single-binary tool
Encourage sustainable work habits via a burnout/sickness mechanic rather than pure grind-rewarding
Deliver a charming, high-craft pet experience (ASCII/pixel art, animations) that differentiates from generic git-stats CLIs
Support extensibility via integrations (GitHub/GitLab), notifications, and social sharing in later versions
target_users: Individual software developers who want a fun, low-friction way to track their coding activity
Solo devs and hobbyist coders motivated by gamification and visual feedback
Engineering teams interested in lightweight, opt-in shared/social productivity fun
Developers prone to overworking who could benefit from a gentle, ambient wellbeing nudge
vision.problem_statement: Developers already generate rich activity data (commits, CLI usage, deploys) but this data is typically buried in dashboards and analytics tools that people rarely open twice, providing no emotional or ambient connection to their own productivity or wellbeing. There's no lightweight, always-visible way to feel connected to one's daily momentum without it becoming another guilt-inducing analytics tool.
success_metrics: Number of active installs / daily active pets (daemon running)
Retention: percentage of users still running tamagotui after 30/60/90 days
Average session frequency of glancing at or checking the widget/status
Adoption rate of git hook and shell activity integrations per user
User-reported reduction in overwork/burnout incidents tied to the sickness mechanic
Engagement with v2 features (snapshots shared, breeding pairs created, notifications enabled)
GitHub stars, Homebrew installs, and community contributions as proxy for organic growth

services.name: sync_api
services.description: Opt-in cloud gateway for Tamagotui. Handles device/user auth, syncing local pet state and event logs to the cloud, leaderboard queries, and breeding/pairing seed exchange between teammates. Core hub that other backend services publish events into.
responsibilities: Authenticate devices/users via lightweight token-based auth for opt-in cloud sync
Accept and persist pet state snapshots and event logs pushed from local clients
Serve leaderboard queries (aggregate XP/streaks across opted-in users/teams)
Handle breeding/pairing requests between two teammates' pets via shared seed hash
Consume events published by integrations_poller and merge them into a user's event log
Expose API for snapshot_service to fetch current pet state for rendering
Rate limit and cache hot leaderboard/read paths via Redis

dependencies.description: Durable storage for pet state, event logs, users, and leaderboard data
Leaderboard caching, rate limiting, and consuming integration events via streams
Receives feed events (PR merges, issue closures, CI results) published asynchronously

frontend.design_notes: Tamagotui's web app is the companion 'window into the tank' for a tool that primarily lives on the CLI/desktop widget — so the SPA should feel like a cozy, ambient terminal-adjacent space, not a SaaS dashboard. Visual language: dark charcoal/near-black backgrounds (#0d0f12) with a single warm accent (amber/egg-yolk #f5a623) and a secondary mint (#7ee8c1) for 'healthy' states, red-orange for burnout warnings. Typography pairs a monospace face (JetBrains Mono / IBM Plex Mono) for stats/numbers with a rounded friendly sans (e.g. Quicksand or Nunito) for pet dialogue/copy — mixing 'terminal precision' with 'creature warmth'. The pet itself is rendered as animated pixel-art sprite sheets (CSS sprite animation or canvas) with idle/eat/sleep/evolve/sick animation states — this is the emotional centerpiece and should have a dedicated large stage area with a subtle parallax/particle background (floating pixels, soft glow pulsing with heartbeat rate tied to activity level). Layout is a hybrid: a persistent minimal top bar (not a heavy sidebar) since the star of the show is the pet stage, with a slide-out drawer for secondary nav (devices, team, settings). Use shadcn/ui primitives (Card, Dialog, Sheet, Tabs, Toast, DropdownMenu) skinned with rounded-2xl corners, soft shadows, and micro-interactions (framer-motion) — evolution moments deserve a full-screen celebratory overlay with confetti/particle burst, not just a toast. Empty/loading states should have personality (the egg wobbling, a 'waiting for signal' shimmer) rather than generic spinners. react-query handles all server cache (pet state, events, leaderboard, teams) with aggressive but short staleTime + a manual 'sync now' affordance, since the real source of truth is local CLI activity being pushed up — the web app is a mirror, and should visually communicate 'last synced X seconds ago'. Mobile: fully responsive but treated as a secondary surface — a simplified single-column 'check on your pet' view, since primary usage is desktop-adjacent glancing.
frontend.theme: shadcn/ui + tailwind, dark-mode-first with a pixel-art accent layer

clients.description: Client for the sync_api service (go) handling auth, users, devices, pet state sync, events, teams, leaderboard, and breeding. Throws `HatchlingApiError` (or `AuthError` for 401s after refresh fails) for non-2xx responses; network failures throw `TypeError`/`HatchlingApiError` with code 'NETWORK_ERROR'.

methods.name: refreshToken

methods.name: listDevices

methods.description: Removes a registered device by id. Throws HatchlingApiError code 'NOT_FOUND' if the device doesn't exist or isn't owned by the caller.

methods.name: updateMe

methods.name: deleteMe
methods.description: Permanently deletes the authenticated user's account and data. Irreversible; clears local TokenStore on success.

methods.name: pushEvents

shared_types: export interface ApiError { code: string; message: string; statusCode: number; details?: Record<string, unknown>; }
export class HatchlingApiError extends Error { readonly statusCode: number; readonly code: string; readonly details?: Record<string, unknown>; constructor(err: ApiError); }
export class AuthError extends HatchlingApiError {}
export interface Paginated<T> { items: T[]; nextCursor?: string | null; totalCount?: number; }
export interface TokenPair { accessToken: string; refreshToken: string; expiresAt: string; }
export interface TokenStore { getAccessToken(): Promise<string | null>; getRefreshToken(): Promise<string | null>; setTokens(tokens: TokenPair): Promise<void>; clear(): Promise<void>; }
export interface HealthStatus { status: 'ok' | 'degraded' | 'down'; version?: string; timestamp: string; }
export interface RegisterRequest { email: string; password: string; deviceName?: string; }
export interface LoginRequest { email: string; password: string; }
export interface AuthResponse extends TokenPair { userId: string; }
export interface Device { id: string; userId: string; name: string; platform: string; createdAt: string; lastSeenAt?: string; }
export interface RegisterDeviceRequest { name: string; platform: string; pushToken?: string; }

sdk.auth_pattern: Bearer token via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Tokens are held in-memory by a `TokenStore` object passed into (or created by) the top-level `HatchlingClient`. The client never persists tokens to disk itself; callers may supply a custom storage adapter (e.g. keychain, encrypted file) via `TokenStore` interface (`{ getAccessToken(), getRefreshToken(), setTokens(), clear() }`). All service clients share the same `TokenStore` instance. On any request receiving a 401, the underlying `HttpTransport` automatically attempts a single `POST /auth/refresh` using the stored refresh token, updates the store, and retries the original request once before surfacing an `AuthError`.
sdk.base_url_config: Each service client accepts its own `baseUrl` in its constructor options (defaults read from `HatchlingClientConfig.endpoints.{syncApi,snapshotService,integrationsPoller}`), since sync_api, snapshot_service, and integrations_poller are deployed independently. A top-level `HatchlingClient` factory accepts a single config object `{ endpoints: { syncApi, snapshotService, integrationsPoller }, tokenStore?, fetch? }` and constructs/wires all three clients with a shared `HttpTransport` (custom `fetch` implementation injectable for testing/SSR/node).

adrs.title: Local-first storage with embedded SQLite as source of truth
adrs.context: Tamagotui's core value proposition is an offline, zero-dependency ambient pet driven by local dev activity (git hooks, shell activity, manual events). The MVP must work with no server and no account. However we still need structured growth history, event logs, and queryable stats (streaks, XP curve, evolution thresholds) rather than a flat JSON blob, to support v2 features like species variety and burnout detection which need windowed queries over event history.
adrs.decision: Use an embedded SQLite database (via mattn/go-sqlite3 or modernc.org/sqlite for cgo-free builds) at ~/.tamagotui/state.db as the single local source of truth for pet state, event log, and growth history. Drop the plain state.json approach except possibly as a one-time export/debug artifact.
adrs.rationale: SQLite gives us transactional writes (important since git hooks and shell pings can fire concurrently), simple time-windowed queries for decay/burnout logic, and a well-understood embedded format with zero external services. It keeps the 'single static binary, fully offline' philosophy intact while giving us room to grow schema-wise for v2 features.
consequences: All CLI commands and the daemon must coordinate DB access safely (single daemon process owns writes; CLI subcommands talk to daemon via local socket rather than opening the DB directly, avoiding SQLite lock contention).
Adds a small binary size / cgo complexity trade-off unless a pure-Go SQLite driver is used.
Enables straightforward local analytics (streaks, XP curves) via SQL without hand-rolled JSON parsing.
Migration tooling (simple embedded SQL migrations) is needed as schema evolves across versions.

adrs.title: Background daemon + thin CLI/TUI clients communicating over a local Unix socket
adrs.context: The pet must react live to git commits, shell activity pings, and idle decay ticks, while also being observable via `tamagotui watch` (persistent widget) and `tamagotui status` (one-off CLI). Multiple processes (git hook, shell wrapper, TUI, tray widget) need to feed events into and read state from a single consistent brain without corrupting the SQLite file via concurrent writers.
adrs.decision: Run a single long-lived background daemon process (`tamagotuid`) that owns the SQLite connection, runs the XP/decay/burnout state machine, and exposes a local Unix domain socket (named pipe on Windows) with a small RPC protocol (length-prefixed JSON or gob). All other components (git post-commit hook, shell alias, `tamagotui status`, `tamagotui watch` TUI, tray widget) are thin clients that connect to this socket to push events or pull current state.
adrs.rationale: Centralizing state mutation in one process eliminates SQLite write contention and race conditions between concurrent event sources (a commit and a shell ping arriving simultaneously). It also lets long-running clients (the watch widget) subscribe to a live state-change stream instead of polling the DB directly, giving the 'ambient, always-updating' feel the product needs.
consequences: Requires a daemon lifecycle story: auto-start on `tamagotui init`/`watch`, supervisor/relaunch behavior, and a `tamagotui doctor` check for 'is daemon running/socket reachable'.
Adds minor complexity vs. a single monolithic CLI, but is necessary once multiple concurrent writers (git hooks, shell pings) exist.
Enables a clean seam later for the sync_api client: the daemon becomes the single place that batches and pushes events to the cloud when opted in.
Windows support requires named pipes instead of Unix sockets, adding a small platform abstraction layer.

adrs.title: Opt-in cloud sync via dedicated sync_api with device-token auth, decoupled from local core loop
adrs.context: Cloud features (leaderboards, breeding/pairing with teammates, cross-device history, snapshot sharing) are explicitly optional per the local-first philosophy, but still need real auth and multi-tenant data separation once a user opts in. sync_api is described as the 'core hub that other backend services publish events into,' meaning integrations_poller and snapshot_service both depend on it rather than talking to each other directly.
adrs.decision: Implement sync_api as a Go service with device-code based authentication (CLI-initiated OAuth-device-flow-style pairing producing a long-lived device token stored locally, no passwords required). sync_api is the sole system of record for cloud state (user/device identity, synced event logs, leaderboard aggregates, breeding seed exchange) and the sole ingress point other backend services (integrations_poller, snapshot_service) publish events or requests through. The local daemon pushes a compact, batched, idempotent event stream to sync_api only when cloud sync is explicitly enabled via `tamagotui login`/config flag.
adrs.rationale: Device-flow auth matches a CLI-first tool well (no browser-embedded credential entry in-terminal) and keeps zero-trust boundaries simple. Funneling all backend services through sync_api rather than allowing integrations_poller or snapshot_service to write to a shared DB directly keeps a single well-defined API contract, simplifies auth/authorization enforcement, and lets the local-first core remain completely unaware of cloud internals — the daemon only ever speaks to one endpoint.
consequences: Cloud opt-in users get a single clear point of trust/revocation (device tokens can be individually revoked from sync_api).

integrations_poller and snapshot_service must be built as internal API clients of sync_api rather than sharing its database, requiring sync_api to expose sufficient internal/service-to-service endpoints (with service auth, e.g. mTLS or service API keys, distinct from user device tokens).
Adds moderate latency/coupling for features like snapshot generation (must round-trip through sync_api) but keeps a clean, auditable boundary.

Requires building and operating a small amount of real backend infrastructure (Postgres, service auth) purely for the opt-in slice of users, which must be clearly isolated so it never becomes a dependency for MVP offline usage.

adrs.title: PostgreSQL as the cloud system of record, separate from local SQLite schema
adrs.context: sync_api needs multi-user, multi-device relational storage for accounts/devices, synced event logs, leaderboard aggregation queries, and breeding/pairing seed records — a very different scaling and query profile than the single-user embedded SQLite file used locally.
adrs.decision: Use PostgreSQL as the primary datastore for sync_api, with a schema independent from (but semantically mappable to) the local SQLite event log schema. sync_api owns migrations for this schema; local SQLite and cloud Postgres are never directly linked (sync happens only via the sync_api's public/internal APIs, never via DB replication).
adrs.rationale: Postgres is a proven, low-friction choice for the relational, multi-tenant workload (users, devices, events, leaderboard aggregates, pairing records) and integrates well with Go via standard drivers/ORMs (pgx/sqlc). Keeping local and cloud schemas independent preserves the local-first guarantee: the local product functions fully even if the cloud schema evolves or the service is down.
consequences: Requires a translation/mapping layer in the daemon's sync client and in sync_api's ingestion endpoint between local event shapes and the cloud schema.
Enables standard Postgres tooling (indexes, materialized views) for leaderboard queries without impacting local performance.
Introduces standard operational overhead (backups, migrations, connection pooling) but only for the opt-in cloud slice, not the core product.
Future schema drift between local and cloud representations must be explicitly versioned in the sync protocol to avoid silent data loss during sync.

adrs.title: Python for integrations_poller, isolated from the Go core via sync_api's event ingestion API
adrs.context: integrations_poller needs to poll GitHub/GitLab APIs on a schedule for opted-in users/repos and translate results (PR merges, issue closures, CI status) into Tamagotui feed events. This is an I/O-bound, integration-heavy workload where Python's ecosystem (requests/httpx, existing GitHub/GitLab SDKs, APScheduler/Celery-style schedulers) offers faster iteration than Go, even though the rest of the stack is Go.
adrs.decision: Implement integrations_poller as a standalone Python service that authenticates to sync_api using a service credential, polls external Git hosting APIs per opted-in repo on a schedule, and pushes normalized feed events to sync_api's internal event ingestion endpoint (the same conceptual event shape the local daemon pushes for git/shell activity).
adrs.rationale: Using Python here isolates language-choice risk: the rest of the system (daemon, CLI, sync_api, snapshot_service) stays in Go for single-binary distribution and performance, while integrations_poller — a purely backend, opt-in, non-latency-critical batch/poll worker — can use Python's mature API client ecosystem without affecting core product distribution.
consequences: Two languages now exist in the backend surface, requiring separate CI/build/deploy pipelines and on-call familiarity with both Go and Python service patterns.
sync_api's ingestion API must be language-agnostic and well-documented (OpenAPI) since it is now consumed by both a Go daemon and a Python worker.
Rate-limit handling, backoff, and per-repo polling cadence live entirely in integrations_poller, keeping this complexity out of sync_api and the local daemon.
This service has zero impact on offline/local-only users since it only activates for opted-in cloud-connected repos.

tech_choices.core_cli_daemon: Go — single static cross-platform binary (macOS/Linux/Windows), fast startup, matches 'always running, zero dependency' local-first goal.
tech_choices.tui_rendering: Charm Bubble Tea + Lip Gloss — expressive, animatable terminal UI ideal for ASCII/pixel pet sprites and smooth evolution transitions.
tech_choices.persistent_widget: Fyne or systray (Go) — lightweight native always-on-top window/tray icon so the pet isn't trapped inside a terminal emulator.
tech_choices.local_storage: Embedded SQLite (mattn/go-sqlite3 or modernc.org/sqlite) — transactional, queryable local event/growth log, zero external services.
tech_choices.local_ipc: Unix domain socket (named pipe on Windows) with length-prefixed JSON/gob RPC — coordinates git hook, shell wrapper, CLI, TUI, and tray widget through one daemon.
tech_choices.git_integration: Native Go git hook installer writing .git/hooks/post-commit, plus `git log` shell-out for history backfill on init.
tech_choices.shell_activity_tracking: Injected shell function/alias in .zshrc/.bashrc pinging the daemon's local socket on each CLI invocation.
tech_choices.notifications: gen2brain/beeep — cross-platform native desktop notifications for hatch/evolution/hunger events.
tech_choices.cloud_gateway_service: sync_api (Go, e.g. using Fiber/Chi) — device-token auth, event sync, leaderboard queries, breeding/pairing seed exchange; central hub for backend services.
tech_choices.cloud_datastore: PostgreSQL — relational store for accounts, devices, synced events, leaderboard aggregates, pairing records.
tech_choices.snapshot_rendering: snapshot_service (Go) — composes animated GIF/PNG exports of pet state for social sharing, using Go imaging/GIF encoding libraries.
tech_choices.integrations_worker: integrations_poller (Python, e.g. httpx + APScheduler) — polls GitHub/GitLab APIs, normalizes events, pushes to sync_api.
tech_choices.distribution: Homebrew tap, `go install`, and prebuilt binaries via GoReleaser for the core client; containerized deploys (Docker) for sync_api, snapshot_service, and integrations_poller.

architecture.system_diagram_description: Two clearly separated zones: LOCAL (default, offline) and CLOUD (opt-in). LOCAL zone on the user's machine: a background daemon (tamagotuid) owns an embedded SQLite database and runs the pet's state machine (XP, decay, burnout). It exposes a local Unix socket that four thin clients talk to: (1) the git post-commit hook, (2) the injected shell alias pinging on CLI usage, (3) the `tamagotui status`/`init`/`doctor` CLI commands, and (4) the persistent `tamagotui watch` TUI (Bubble Tea) plus an optional native tray/Fyne widget — both rendering the live pet. This entire LOCAL zone functions fully with zero network access. CLOUD zone, reached only if the user opts in via `tamagotui login`: the daemon batches and pushes events over HTTPS to sync_api (Go), which authenticates devices via device-token flow and persists to PostgreSQL (users, devices, synced event log, leaderboard aggregates, pairing/breeding seeds). sync_api is the sole hub other backend services integrate through. snapshot_service (Go) receives requests (via sync_api or directly with a service token) to render a pet's current state into an animated GIF/PNG for `tamagotui snapshot --share`, reading current state via sync_api and returning a shareable image. integrations_poller (Python) runs independently on a schedule, polling GitHub/GitLab APIs for opted-in repos, and pushes normalized feed events (PR merged, issue closed, CI status) into sync_api's internal ingestion endpoint, from which they flow back down to the relevant user's local daemon on next sync. Arrows: git hook/shell/CLI/TUI → daemon → SQLite (local, always). daemon ⇄ sync_api → PostgreSQL (only if opted-in). integrations_poller → sync_api (service auth). sync_api ⇄ snapshot_service (render requests). All cloud arrows are dashed/optional to visually distinguish from the solid, always-on local core loop.

infrastructure.deployment_target: Kubernetes cluster (or ECS) running containerized sync_api, snapshot_service, and integrations_poller, built via Docker/GoReleaser and deployed behind a load balancer; core CLI/TUI distributed independently via Homebrew/go install/binaries
suggested_managed_services: Managed PostgreSQL (e.g. AWS RDS / GCP Cloud SQL)
Object storage for snapshot exports (S3 / GCS)
Managed Kubernetes (EKS/GKE) or ECS Fargate for service orchestration
Managed load balancer / API gateway for sync_api ingress
Scheduled task runner (e.g. Cloud Scheduler or K8s CronJob) to trigger integrations_poller if not using APScheduler in-process
Centralized logging/monitoring (Datadog, CloudWatch, or Grafana Loki + Prometheus)
Secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager / Vault) for JWT and API credentials
infrastructure.scaling_notes: sync_api is the primary scaling bottleneck as user base grows: scale horizontally behind a load balancer, use connection pooling to PostgreSQL, and add Redis caching for leaderboard/read-heavy queries. snapshot_service is CPU/memory-bound (image/GIF encoding) — scale as a separate worker pool or use async job queue with autoscaling based on queue depth. integrations_poller should run as a single scheduled/coordinated worker (or leader-elected replica) to avoid duplicate API polling against GitHub/GitLab rate limits; consider a job queue (e.g. Redis-backed) to distribute polling tasks per integration/user. Local CLI/daemon components require no server-side scaling as they run entirely on-device.
